title: I Got Pickpocketed in Lisbon (What I Did Next)
creator: Ruth Abernathy
description:
Day 4 in Lisbon and my phone is gone. Here's everything that happened and everything I'd do differently.

This video is sponsored by Airvo. Get 15% off your first eSIM with code RUTH15 at https://airvo.com

Where I stayed: a tiny guesthouse in Graça
Camera: an old mirrorless and a cheap mic

sentences.t: So I'm sitting on a bench in Graça right now, and I want to tell you about the worst morning of this whole trip.
It was day four, and I was doing the most touristy thing you can do in Lisbon, which is ride the twenty eight tram.
If you've done it, you know, it's packed, it's hot, everyone is pressed together like sardines.
And I had my phone in the back pocket of my shorts, which, yes, I know.
I know.
We go round this really tight corner, there's a little shove, a guy says sorry, and I think nothing of it.
Two stops later I reach for my phone to film the view and it's just gone.
Honestly my first feeling wasn't even panic, it was this weird embarrassment, like, of course it was me.
Then the panic arrived.
Because my phone was my boarding passes, my bank app, my hotel booking, my maps, everything.
I got off the tram and just stood on the pavement for a minute trying to remember anybody's phone number.
I could not remember a single one, not even my mum's.
So I walked to a police station, which was its own adventure, and filed a report with a very kind officer who spoke amazing English.
Then I bought the cheapest phone I could find in a shop near Rossio.
But then came the real nightmare, because my number back home was tied to a physical SIM that was now in some stranger's pocket.
My bank kept trying to text a code to a phone I didn't have.
It took me three full days to get a working number and get back into my accounts.
And that whole mess is exactly why, these days, I set up a travel eSIM before I even leave home.
The one I've been using all year is Airvo, and they're sponsoring today's video.
Airvo gives you local data in over a hundred and fifty countries, and you install it straight from the app before your flight.
You land, you switch it on, and you've got data, no hunting for a SIM shop in the airport.
And because it's digital, your home SIM can stay safe in a drawer back home, so nobody on a tram can walk off with it.
The plans are way cheaper than roaming, Portugal is a few euros for a whole week.
Use code RUTH15 at airvo.com to get fifteen percent off your first eSIM.
Anyway, back to the stolen phone saga.
The weirdest part is what happened on day six.
I got an email from the guesthouse saying someone had dropped off a phone at the front desk.
It was mine.
Cracked screen, SIM card gone, but otherwise fine.
The owner said a teenage boy had handed it in and said he found it in a bin near the tram stop.
I don't know if that's true, and I don't really care, I just bought that boy a pastel de nata in my head.
So, what would I do differently?
One, front pocket or a zipped bag on crowded trams, always, no exceptions.
Two, write down two or three phone numbers on a piece of paper in your wallet.
Three, have backup codes for your bank and your email saved somewhere that isn't your phone.
And four, get to the twenty eight early in the morning, at the first stop, when it's actually empty.
Which I did, on my last day, and it was magical.
I had a whole bench to myself and the light was coming down the hill all golden.
Lisbon, you broke my heart a little, but I still love you.
If you've ever been pickpocketed abroad, tell me your story in the comments so I feel less alone.
Next week we're heading down to the Algarve, so make sure you're subscribed.
Bye for now.
